Hi Rafael — thanks for the clear list. A few points from Redwood's side: 

1) Default approach: we prefer beneficiary (Redwood) to receive the gross invoice amount in USD. That keeps our ledger simple and avoids us having to calculate variable correspondent fees for VAT/expense accounting. If Atlas's pool deducts a correspondent fee on route, we ask Atlas to either:
   - absorb the fee (preferred for smaller, non-enterprise customers), or
   - apply a fixed per-invoice fee that you pass to Redwood as a separate line item on the invoice (so it's auditable).

2) Fee floor: if Atlas requires a minimum correspondent fee, we can accept a fee floor model but need it to be explicit in the remittance advice (we cannot reverse-charge unexpectedly). For example, a disclosed "correspondent fee" line on the payment receipt and invoice reconciliation box.

3) Routing preference: Palo Alto/US cover is fine for faster USD credits, but for BRL we recommend using your São Paulo nostro for onshore collections then a single FX conversion on a scheduled settlement window — that reduces multi-hop correspondent deductions. If you route via US cover, please confirm the correspondent chain and expected fixed deductions so we can code the reconciliation rule.

4) VAT / tax handling: Redwood issues invoices net of Brazilian taxes (we don't register local VAT in BRL), so please provide a copy of the remittance showing any taxes withheld by banks (if present). We need a stamped remittance to reconcile with our AP ledger.

I've attached a short matrix (proposed-fee-floor-matrix.xlsx) that shows acceptable fee ranges by invoice size. Can Atlas Treasury review and mark the preferred option (Absorb / Disclose-as-line-item / Gross-up)?

Next steps: if Atlas can mark the matrix and confirm the preferred routing (Nostro BRL vs US cover), we can finalize the invoice template and push the first batch.

Kimberly — thanks for the quick reply and the matrix. We reviewed internally and here's our proposed approach: 

- For invoices under BRL 15,000 (approx USD 3,000), Atlas will absorb a single fixed correspondent deduction up to BRL 45. 
- For invoices BRL 15,000+, Atlas will disclose intermediary fees as a separate line on remittance advice. Atlas prefers not to gross-up by default unless Redwood requires it for a specific customer by contract.
- Routing: we'll default to São Paulo nostro for collection and a scheduled weekly FX conversion to USD. For large enterprise customers we can request a US cover/clean USD delivery if Redwood requests explicitly.

I've attached an updated wire template and marked the fee policy in the comments. Can you confirm Redwood is OK with the two-tier treatment and the requirement for a remittance line for disclosed fees?
